findings.title: Unauthenticated zlib decompression bomb via Serializer.loads_unsafe can OOM the server
findings.description: Entry: src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:349 (Serializer.loads_unsafe), which forwards the unverified payload to load_payload at src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:392; the same path is shown in docs/serializer.rst:52-64 where load_payload(e.payload) is called on a BadSignature payload. Attacker: an outside caller who can send a token to an application that decodes unverified tokens (loads_unsafe, or the documented failure-inspection pattern), crossing the signature-validation boundary that Serializer.loads normally enforces. Path: loads_unsafe(s) -> _loads_unsafe_impl -> self.load_payload(e.payload) (serializer.py:392) -> URLSafeSerializerMixin.load_payload -> base64_decode(payload) -> zlib.decompress(json) at url_safe.py:46 -> json.loads on the expanded bytes. Nothing on this path stops it: loads_unsafe intentionally skips the HMAC check, base64_decode only shrinks the data (4/3 ratio), and zlib.decompress is called with no max_length, output-size check, or payload-size limit anywhere in the library; the decompressed result is then handed to _CompactJSON.loads, adding CPU cost proportional to the expanded size. In the safe loads() path the HMAC verification at signer.py:239 blocks forged payloads, so this amplification is reachable through the unauthenticated decode API and the documented pattern of inspecting BadSignature.payload. Impact: deflate expands up to roughly 1032:1, so a few-KB token (e.g., an 8 KB request line/cookie) turns into megabytes of process memory plus JSON-parsing work per request, and repeated or concurrent requests exhaust memory/CPU and can OOM-kill the server process handling untrusted tokens. Fix: decompress with a bounded output, e.g. use zlib.decompressobj().decompress(data, max_length) and raise BadPayload when the cap is exceeded (or reject payloads above a configured size before decompression), so load_payload and loads_unsafe can no longer expand unauthenticated input without limit.
